schema.label: What each group means
schema.help: Claude uses these to put new tasks in the right group.

schema.label: Email rulebook
schema.help: How FloatBoard judges email. Starts as the built-in rulebook; edit it freely, restore any earlier version, or reset it to the built-in one.

schema.label: Chat rulebook
schema.help: How FloatBoard judges WhatsApp and WeChat messages. Starts as the built-in rulebook; edit it freely, restore any earlier version, or reset it to the built-in one.

schema.label: Your rules
schema.help: Plain words, one rule per line, for everything FloatBoard reads. To aim a rule at one place, start it with Email:, WhatsApp: or Meetings:. Your rules win over the built-in rulebook.

schema.label: What FloatBoard has learned about you
schema.help: Built from your corrections. You can edit it.

schema.label: Your WhatsApp rules (older)
schema.help: Kept from before: these now belong in Your rules, each line starting with WhatsApp:.

schema.label: Never make tasks from
schema.help: Email addresses or @domains, one per line. Their emails are skipped before Claude sees them (free and exact).

schema.label: Always check
schema.help: Email addresses or @domains, one per line, that Claude always judges, even when Gmail files them under Promotions or Updates (which are normally skipped).

schema.label: Mark the email read when I finish its task
End reply drafts with "Assisted by AI"
schema.help: Adds an italic Assisted by AI line at the end of every reply draft.

schema.label: Send urgent tasks to your phone
Judge messages and learn with
schema.help: Haiku is fast and costs very little. Sonnet is more careful and costs about 20 times more.

schema.label: Update what was learned after every
schema.help: corrections (each task you delete as not needed, or change). Until then, recent corrections are already shown to Claude with every message.
